meta.name: Sourdough Chocolate Chip Cookies

source.name: Research Synthesis (40 sources)
source.author: Primary influences: Caroline Schiff (King Arthur Baking), Edd Kimber (The Boy Who Bakes)

meta.total_time: ~17 hrs (30 min active Day 1, 16-24 hr overnight rest, 30 min active Day 2)
meta.description: Brown butter sourdough chocolate chip cookies with overnight ferment. All-butter (no oil), egg yolks only, hand-chopped chocolate. The sourdough tang pairs with brown butter's nuttiness and dark chocolate's bitterness.

states.title: Brown the Butter
states.direction: In a light-colored saucepan over medium-high heat, melt butter and cook, whisking frequently and scraping the bottom, until a light honey color with brown bits forming on the bottom, 4-6 minutes. Remove from heat and cool 5 minutes.
states.exit_condition: Butter is honey-colored with visible brown flecks on the bottom; nutty aroma; yields approximately 185g

notes.text: Use a light-colored pan so you can see the color change. Dark pans hide the browning and make it easy to burn.
Pull off heat slightly early — residual heat continues browning. If you smell burnt or acrid notes, start over with fresh butter.

states.title: Chill Brown Butter
states.direction: Transfer brown butter to a small bowl. Cover and refrigerate until opaque and creamy in consistency, about 1 hour.
states.exit_condition: Brown butter is opaque, creamy, and holds its shape — not liquid, not rock-hard

notes.text: This step is critical. Warm brown butter melts sugar on contact, creating greasy dough that spreads too thin in the oven. The butter should feel like softened butter when ready.

states.title: Mix Butter and Sugars
states.direction: In a large mixing bowl, combine the chilled brown butter with dark brown sugar and granulated sugar. Mix with a spatula or wooden spoon until evenly combined, about 2 minutes.
states.exit_condition: Butter and sugars are evenly combined with a wet, sandy appearance

notes.text: No stand mixer needed. Since the brown butter is already pre-melted (just chilled), there is no creaming step — you are simply combining, not aerating.

states.title: Add Egg Yolks
states.direction: Add egg yolks one at a time, mixing well after each addition until fully incorporated.
states.exit_condition: Each yolk fully incorporated before adding the next; mixture is smooth and glossy

notes.text: Yolks only (no whites). Whites add water and protein structure that makes cookies cakey. Yolks add fat and lecithin for a fudgier, chewier cookie.

states.title: Add Discard and Vanilla
states.direction: Add sourdough discard and vanilla extract. Mix until smooth and fully incorporated.
states.exit_condition: Mixture is smooth and homogeneous; no streaks of discard visible

notes.text: Use discard that is 1-5 days old at 100% hydration (by weight). Very old or sour discard can over-acidify the dough. Over-hydrated starter leads to flat, greasy cookies.

states.title: Whisk Dry Ingredients
states.direction: In a medium bowl, whisk together all-purpose flour, bread flour, baking soda, baking powder, and fine sea salt.
states.exit_condition: Dry ingredients evenly combined with no visible clumps

notes.text: The AP + bread flour blend adds chewiness from bread flour's higher protein while keeping cookies tender from the AP flour. Most sourdough CCC blogs use AP only — the blend is our differentiator.

states.title: Combine Dough
states.direction: Add the dry ingredients to the wet mixture in 2-3 additions, folding with a rubber spatula until just combined after each addition. Stop as soon as no visible dry flour streaks remain.
states.exit_condition: No visible dry flour streaks; dough is cohesive but not overworked

notes.text: Do not overmix. Overmixing develops too much gluten, making cookies tough and cakey. Stop the moment flour disappears.

states.title: Fold in Chocolate
states.direction: Using a rubber spatula, fold 300g of the chopped chocolate into the dough until evenly distributed. Reserve the remaining 50g for pressing into tops before baking.
states.exit_condition: Chocolate evenly distributed throughout dough; reserved chocolate set aside

notes.text: Hand-chopped bar chocolate creates irregular pieces — thin shavings melt into pools while larger chunks stay semi-intact. This gives different chocolate experiences in every bite.

states.title: Overnight Rest
states.direction: Cover the bowl tightly with plastic wrap pressed directly onto the dough surface. Refrigerate for 16-24 hours.
states.exit_condition: Dough has rested minimum 16 hours; is firm and cold throughout

notes.text: The overnight rest is non-negotiable. It serves dual purpose: flour hydration and fat solidification for texture, plus slow sourdough fermentation for flavor depth. The critical inflection point is at 16 hours (Nik Sharma).
Dough can rest up to 48 hours. Beyond that, diminishing returns and potential over-fermentation.

states.title: Preheat Oven
states.direction: Position rack in upper third of oven, about 15cm from the top heating element. Preheat to 350°F (175°C). Line baking sheets with parchment paper.
states.exit_condition: Oven reaches 350°F (175°C) and baking sheets are lined with parchment

states.title: Scoop and Shape Cookies
states.direction: Using a cookie scoop, portion dough into 57g balls. Roll gently into balls, then press reserved chopped chocolate into the tops. Place on parchment-lined baking sheets, spaced 8cm apart. No more than 6 cookies per sheet.
states.exit_condition: Dough portioned into uniform 57g balls with chocolate pressed into tops; maximum 6 per sheet with 8cm spacing

notes.text: Pressing chocolate into the surface creates visible chocolate puddles on the baked cookie exterior — a signature bakery technique from Caroline Schiff.
Freeze extra dough balls on a sheet, then transfer to a zip bag. Bake from frozen — add 2-3 minutes to bake time. Frozen dough keeps up to 2 months.

states.title: Bake
states.direction: Bake one sheet at a time for 12-14 minutes, until edges are golden brown and centers appear slightly underbaked and puffy.
states.exit_condition: Edges golden brown, centers look slightly underbaked and puffy; cookies still soft when gently pressed

notes.text: Cookies firm up significantly as they cool. Pull them when they still look underdone in the center — they continue baking on the hot sheet.
Let baking sheets cool completely between batches. Hot sheets cause immediate spreading.

states.title: Salt and Cool
states.direction: Immediately sprinkle flaky sea salt over the warm cookies. Cool on the baking sheet for 15 minutes, then transfer to a wire rack.
states.exit_condition: Cookies are set and firm enough to handle; salt has adhered to warm surface

cook_log.summary: Split-batch first bake — 6 cookies same-night via 30-min freezer chill, 19 cookies from rested dough next morning (25 total, recipe target 22-24). Subbed 60g Ryman Rye for AP (BSM heritage experiment). Brown butter pulled cautious (lighter than ideal); same-night batch needed 15-20 min vs recipe 12-14, came out good.
notes: Wed 8:10pm — Made brown butter, cooling. Possibly under-browned; pulled cautious to avoid burning.
Wed 8:59pm — Used 60g Ryman Rye (sub from AP flour) as experiment.
Wed 9:37pm — Mixed dough. Into Cambro, fridge. Scooped 6 cookies for night bake; freezing 30 min.
Wed 10:48pm — Night batch baked 15-20 min total (recipe calls for 12-14). Came out good. Wondering if oven temp could go higher for more browning.
Thu 11:34am — Started morning bakes ~9am from rested dough. Two batches of 6 done so far; second batch cooling.
Thu 12:02pm — Last batch ended up 7 cookies (2 measured 59g; all other batches were 57g exactly). Total yield: 25 cookies (recipe says 22-24). Recipe yield is pretty close.

next_time.text: Brown butter deeper next time — pull at nutty aroma + visible brown flecks on bottom. Light brown butter likely contributed to pale finish + longer bake.
Try raising oven temp 10-15°F (or shift rack lower) for more browning. Same-night batch needed 15-20 min vs recipe 12-14.
A/B taste compare: same-night freezer-chill batch vs ~12-hr rested morning batch. Log differences after cooling.
Scoop discipline: 4 batches all hit 57g exactly except final batch (2 cookies at 59g). Last-scoop drift is normal — fine to accept, or split into 8 smaller cookies next time.

cook_log.summary: Heritage-flour experiment, split-batch — first 8 of 24 cookies baked 06-04 evening (~60g each, 14 min from freezer-chilled scoops); visible cracks, likely einkorn. Heritage subs: BSM Marquis 80g + einkorn 119g (50% AP swap). Chocolate trimmed to 250g fold + 50g tops. Dough yielded 1441g. Dry mix overshot recipe v2.0.4 by ~38% (agent mise error citing Clever Carrot original weights); proceeded as-mixed. Cost $19.95 total ($0.91/cookie); chocolate dominates at $11.36.
notes: 2026-06-04 evening — Mixed dry. Marquis weighed 80g (finished the BSM bag). Topped up bread portion with 124g KABF bread flour to hit 204g.
2026-06-04 evening — AP portion: 119g KABF AP + 119g BSM einkorn (50% swap for fun — heritage experiment).
2026-06-04 evening — Leaveners + salt: 4g baking powder, 5g baking soda, 7g fine sea salt. Whisked hard (einkorn clumps).

2026-06-04 evening — Mid-mix discovery: total dry hit 458g (442g flour + 16g leavener/salt). Recipe v2.0.4 actually calls for 320g flour + 13g leavener/salt; agent had cited Clever Carrot original (442g/17g). User chose to proceed as-mixed ("oh well.. lets see how it turns out") rather than scale wet 1.38x or discard 122g dry. Expect cakier rise (BP 2x), drier crumb, possibly less spread (extra flour, einkorn lower hydration draw).
2026-06-04 6:43pm — Folded only 250g chocolate (recipe spec 300g). Judged sufficient. Reserving 50g for tops per recipe.
2026-06-04 9:07pm — Dough chilled a few hours in fridge. Total dough yield 1441g. Doing one set of 6 cookies tonight.
2026-06-04 9:37pm — Started bake. Scoops went into freezer first to chill cold before sheet.
2026-06-04 9:54pm — Out of oven at 14 minutes (cold-from-freezer scoops). Cookies show visible cracks — "probably from einkorn" (lower gluten = less elastic surface).
2026-06-04 9:56pm — Plan: shape and freeze the rest of the dough tomorrow. Tonight's batch was 8 cookies at ~60g each (480g). Targeting 24 total at 60g/each (~1440g) — matches 1441g actual yield.

photos.alt: Eight golden-brown cookies in two rows of four on parchment-lined sheet pan fresh from the oven. Heritage flour bake — BSM Marquis + einkorn experiment, baked 14 min from freezer-chilled scoops.

cook_log.summary: Best-execution cookie bake to date — brown butter dialed to honey color, 250g chocolate fold + ~5-chip decorative tops, ~20 min on large sheet pan at recipe temp. 13 cookies + 1 mini baked; 8 dough balls vacuum-sealed for Thursday.
notes: Mixed dough Fri 07-03 ~20:30 — into fridge overnight.
Chocolate: 250g folded in (intentional). Recipe's 50g 'tops' number treated as decoration only — ~5 chips per cookie, not a weight.
Brown butter dialed to honey color — good this time; a prior attempt a few days ago was overdone.
Out of fridge Sat 07-04 ~11:00; tempered on counter until ~12:00 for easier scooping.
Scoop: target 56g per ball; many landed 57-58g. Divided by 24 but came up ~1.5 cookies short. Dough transfer/scoop was lossless — cambro was clean by end of shaping.
Chilled scooped balls in freezer ~15 min to solidify.
Baked Sat ~12:30 on large sheet pan (vs usual half-sheet which fits only 8); 13 cookies + 1 extra mini fit comfortably.
Bake time ~20 min at recipe temp — pulled by eye.
Remainder: 8 dough balls vacuum-sealed to freezer for Thursday bake.
Verdict: one of the better bakes (taste-test metrics pending).

photos.alt: Cold-rested dough in a square lidded container on parchment with a cookie scoop resting inside; chocolate chunks visible throughout the tan dough after the overnight fridge rest.

Close-up of baked cookies on the wire rack — puffed rounds with molten chocolate chip tops and honey-brown color from the dialed-in brown butter; Great Pyrenees and second dog mid-lick blurred in background.
Rack of finished cookies in the foreground with the Great Pyrenees watching from across the room — decorative chips on each cookie top, honey-brown crumb, edges set but centers still glossy.

Hero shot of the finished bake — wire rack of 13 cookies plus one mini on a large sheet pan, warm honey-brown crumb from the browned butter, chocolate chunks visible across the tops; both dogs framed in the background.

next_time.text: Scoop math: aim ~5g under a perfectly-divisible target (e.g. 51g if dividing dough by 24) — actual scoops drift up to 57-58g, which eats into cookie count. Dough is lossless so under-target is safe.
Recipe 'chocolate tops 50g' field is misleading — for this bake pattern tops are ~5 chips per cookie decoration, not a weight. Clarify in recipe or split into separate ingredient lines.
A/B taste: today's brown-butter-honey batch vs Thursday's frozen-dough batch. Log crumb/edge/flavor differences.
New evaluation metric proposed (from photo tagging): 'dog loitering %' as informal bake success indicator — Pyrenees hovering = kitchen-approved.

techniques.name: Brown butter (all-butter, no oil)
techniques.rationale: Universal consensus. Browning evaporates ~20% water, creating room for sourdough moisture while adding nutty depth.

techniques.name: Egg yolks only
techniques.rationale: Removes water from whites; adds fat and lecithin for fudgier texture. Validated by JennyBlogs bake-off top 2.

techniques.name: Overnight ferment (16-24 hrs)
techniques.rationale: Flour hydration, enzymatic sugar breakdown, sourdough flavor development. Nik Sharma: 16hr inflection point.

techniques.name: Hand-chopped bar chocolate
techniques.rationale: Bar chocolate has more cocoa butter than chips; irregular pieces create varied melt. Reserve some for surface.

techniques.name: Hand mix (no stand mixer)
techniques.rationale: Brown butter is already melted — no creaming step needed. Spatula gives better gluten control.

techniques.name: AP + bread flour blend
techniques.rationale: Most blogs use AP only; KAB and our v1 use the blend. Bread flour adds chew. Our differentiator.

technical_notes.title: Quick Bake vs Overnight Rest
technical_notes.text:
- Recipe defaults to overnight rest (8-24h fridge). Same-day bake works with tradeoffs.
- **Why rest helps**: flour hydrates fully (chewier crumb, less gritty); enzymes break starch into sugars (deeper browning, toffee depth); discard acidity mellows; dough firms so cookies stay thicker (less spread).
- **Quick bake (30-min freezer chill, no overnight)**: flatter cookies (warm butter spreads in oven), paler color (less browning fuel), sharper sourdough tang, slightly grittier bite from under-hydrated flour.
- **Minimum viable chill**: 30 min in freezer firms butter enough to prevent runaway spread. Flavor will be one-dimensional compared to rested dough.
- **No yeast involved**: leavening is baking soda + baking powder. Sourdough discard contributes flavor + hydration, not lift. Adding instant yeast won't help — bake window is too short for fermentation.

technical_notes.title: Split-Batch Workflow (Same-Night + Overnight)
technical_notes.text:
- Best of both: brown butter + mix full dough once, then split between same-night bake and overnight rest. Same dough → two cookies, side-by-side A/B.
- **Tonight portion** (~6 cookies, one sheet — matches per-sheet max): scoop balls, freezer 30 min, bake. Expect flatter, paler, sharper sourdough tang.
- **Tomorrow portion** (remainder, ~17 cookies): press plastic wrap directly onto dough surface in bulk. Refrigerate 16-24h. Scoop + bake next day. Expect deeper toffee, chewier, mellow tang.
- **Bulk-rest the remainder, do not pre-scoop balls then fridge**: smaller surface area on bulk dough → less air exposure → better flour hydration during the rest.
- **Frozen alternative** (if fridge is full): scoop tomorrow's balls now and freeze on a tray. Bake from frozen, +2-3 min. Loses the overnight ferment flavor — use only as last resort.
- **Tomorrow's bake time may shift**: colder, firmer dough may need +1 min. Watch for golden edges + puffy underbaked center (same exit condition as state `bake-cookies`).
